facts.statement: The project .env at the repository root is the single source of truth for installed tool paths (A100_PREFIX, A100_TOOLCHAIN, A100_SYSROOT, A100_CROSS_PREFIX, A100_QEMU, A100_QEMU_CPU, A100_REFERENCE_PYTHON, PYTHONPATH, A100_PUBLIC_REFERENCE_CACHE, A100_NO_PYTHON_IMAGE, COMPILER_WORKFLOW_ATTACK_BROKER); a100_support/env.sh derives the same prefix and run-riscv.sh / run-reference.sh source it. .env declares no measurement/profiling tool and no benchmark entrypoint; none is required under correctness_only.
facts.source: read ./.env and a100_support/env.sh on 2026-11-04; every declared path resolved by the probes recorded in docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md

facts.statement: RISC-V cross compiler /home/i_yinzida/.local/opt/a100/toolchain-1.1.2/bin/riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu-gcc is present and usable: version riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu-gcc (g56971dcbea2) 14.3.0; it built a trivial C program (-O2 -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d) that executed under the declared QEMU endpoint with the expected output A100-C-SMOKE-OK and exit 0.
facts.source: probe: set -a; . ./.env; set +a; ${A100_CROSS_PREFIX}gcc --version; build and run recorded in docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md End-to-end smoke 1

facts.statement: Cross binutils at /home/i_yinzida/.local/opt/a100/toolchain-1.1.2/bin (riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu-as, -ld, -objdump; GNU Binutils 2.43.1.20250119) are present and usable: hand-written rv64gcv assembly was assembled with as and linked with ld into a static ELF that executed under the declared QEMU endpoint with expected output and the guest exit code preserved (42).
facts.source: probe: ${A100_CROSS_PREFIX}as --version; ${A100_CROSS_PREFIX}ld --version; ${A100_CROSS_PREFIX}objdump --version; as/ld build and run in docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md End-to-end smoke 2

facts.statement: The declared sysroot /home/i_yinzida/.local/opt/a100/toolchain-1.1.2/sysroot is present and usable: it contains libc.so.6 and the lp64d dynamic loader (sysroot/lib/ld-linux-riscv64-lp64d.so.1), and a dynamically linked C program ran under QEMU with -L $A100_SYSROOT.

The declared QEMU execution endpoint is present and usable: /home/i_yinzida/.local/opt/a100/jdsk-qemu-10.0.2/bin/qemu-riscv64 reports qemu-riscv64 version 10.0.2 and executes riscv64 ELF under -cpu max,vlen=1024,elen=64,vext_spec=v1.0 with -L sysroot; three fresh smokes (C, hand-written assembly, RVV check) returned their expected outputs and exit codes.
facts.source: probe: $A100_QEMU --version; timeout-bounded runs of smoke_c, smoke_asm and smoke_rvv in docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md

facts.statement: Under the declared CPU model (max,vlen=1024,elen=64,vext_spec=v1.0) the QEMU endpoint provides RVV 1.0 with VLEN=1024: a smoke reading CSR vlenb observed 128 and executed vsetvli, vmv.v.x, vadd.vv and vmv.x.s correctly (exit 0); the same binary under -cpu max,vlen=256,elen=64,vext_spec=v1.0 exited 1, so the observation is real and not vacuous.
facts.source: probe: timeout 60 $A100_QEMU -L $A100_SYSROOT -cpu "$A100_QEMU_CPU" ./a100_support/build/smoke_rvv -> exit 0; control with vlen=256 -> exit 1; docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md End-to-end smoke 3

facts.statement: The native runtime transport is present and usable: a100_support/native_io.py pack_case plus a100_support/run-riscv.sh plus the native_bundle.c runtime (io_fixture) plus unpack_outputs completed a full host-to-QEMU-to-host round trip for a strided-alias case with guest pointer relocation and for a bfloat16 value-storage case, both compared PASS; a100_support.native_device.make_device correctly refuses until A100_COMPILER_FACTORY is set, so there is no reference fallback for candidate execution.
facts.source: probe: timeout 300 python3 a100_support/build/transport_probe.py -> alias comparison PASS, bf16 comparison PASS; build commands in docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md Native runtime transport

facts.statement: Dynamic instruction observation is present and usable: the QEMU 10 plugin API works with a100_support/probes/instruction_counts.c compiled by host gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0) against jdsk-qemu-10.0.2/include and host-runtime-bookworm glib headers; the plugin counted smt.vmadot executions=1 at pc 68508 for the int8 matrix probe and counted zero instructions for a binary without matrix instructions (control).
facts.source: probe: gcc -shared -fPIC ... a100_support/probes/instruction_counts.c -o instruction_counts.so; timeout 90 $A100_QEMU ... -plugin instruction_counts.so,out=ime-int8-counts.json matrix_probe int8; docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md Dynamic instruction observation

facts.statement: A100 IME matrix instructions execute and compare correctly under the declared QEMU endpoint for int8 (fresh 2026-11-04 run: probe int8 passed=true, vlenb=128, one smt.vmadot execution counted); the recorded prep-time probes in docs/compiler-agent/TOOLCHAIN_PROBES.json additionally show int4 and fp16 as EXECUTED_AND_COMPARED_PASS with counted smt.vmadot / smt.vfwmadot executions.
facts.source: probe: timeout 90 $A100_QEMU -L $A100_SYSROOT -cpu "$A100_QEMU_CPU" -plugin instruction_counts.so,out=ime-int8-counts.json matrix_probe int8 -> exit 0; recorded evidence docs/compiler-agent/TOOLCHAIN_PROBES.json matrix rows

facts.statement: The pinned QEMU emulator BF16 IME format selection has not passed and remains unverified: the bf16 matrix probe fails (fresh 2026-11-04 run exit 1, probe bf16 passed=false) while the executed smt.vfwmadot selects the MCPM float16 operand format; FP16 or ordinary vector success cannot prove BF16 IME execution. BF16 cases must be preserved and this instruction-path gap recorded separately.
facts.source: probe: timeout 90 $A100_QEMU ... matrix_probe bf16 -> exit 1, ime-bf16-counts.json shows operand_format MCPM-selected-float16; recorded docs/compiler-agent/TOOLCHAIN_PROBES.json bf16 row UNSUPPORTED_OR_FAILED

facts.statement: The MCPM control CSR is not accessible from userspace under the pinned QEMU: the recorded csr probe returned -4 with zero matrix instruction executions, and every fresh matrix probe reports mcpm_control default-no-userspace-access.
facts.source: probe: mcpm_control field of fresh matrix_probe runs; recorded csr row (returncode -4) in docs/compiler-agent/TOOLCHAIN_PROBES.json

facts.statement: The SpacemiT LLVM package /home/i_yinzida/.local/opt/a100/llvm-spacemit-f6ded0be is present but unusable on this host: llc, opt, llvm-mc, llvm-as, llvm-dis and ld.lld all fail with GLIBC_2.36 / GLIBC_2.38 not found (host glibc too old) and the package contains no clang binary. It is not on the declared build path (.env declares the GCC/binutils cross toolchain), so this is not a blocker for the compiler build path.
facts.source: probe: timeout 20 /home/i_yinzida/.local/opt/a100/llvm-spacemit-f6ded0be/bin/llc --version -> GLIBC_2.38 not found; same error for opt, llvm-mc, llvm-as, llvm-dis, ld.lld; docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md SpacemiT LLVM

facts.statement: The compiled x86 Triton CPU reference environment is present and usable: /home/i_yinzida/.local/opt/a100/venvs/triton-cpu/bin/python (3.12.16) with triton 3.8.0, numpy 2.5.4 and torch 2.15.0+cpu executed a masked vector-add Triton kernel (tail not a multiple of BLOCK) through a100_support/run-reference.sh and compared PASS (fresh 2026-11-04). It is the question-validation service only and never substitutes for candidate target execution.
facts.source: probe: timeout 420 a100_support/run-reference.sh a100_support/build/reference_probe.py -> masked vector-add comparison: PASS; versions match docs/compiler-agent/REFERENCE_ENVIRONMENT.json

tasks.goal: Environment analysis for the A100 correctness-only compiler run: discover and verify, with executed probe evidence, every local capability the chip input's build/execution path requires (RISC-V cross toolchain: cc/as/ld, QEMU riscv64 execution endpoint with the declared CPU model, the native runtime transport in a100_support/, the compiled x86 Triton CPU reference environment, and any host driver Python needs), classify each declared tool as present+usable / present+unusable / absent with the exact command and output, run at least one end-to-end smoke that builds a trivial RISC-V program with the declared toolchain and executes it under the declared QEMU endpoint, record Facts with RUNTIME_PROBE/EMPIRICAL confidence and Assumptions for anything not probed, and record that the project .env is the single source of truth for these paths. Correctness_only scope: no timing/profiling stack, benchmark rate or measured performance is required; verify build/run tools and required resource/instruction observation capabilities instead.
acceptance: Every capability the chip input's execution path needs (cross-compile, assemble/link, QEMU execution, native runtime transport, reference comparison environment, host Python driver) is classified present+usable, present+unusable, or absent, each backed by the exact probe command and its output recorded as evidence.

At least one end-to-end smoke (build a trivial program with the declared cross toolchain and run it under the declared QEMU endpoint) has executed successfully and is recorded as evidence with its command and output.

Tool paths and versions are recorded as Facts with RUNTIME_PROBE or EMPIRICAL confidence and provenance naming the probe command; anything not probed is recorded as an Assumption with a validation method, and no unavailable claim exists without an attempted command and its error.
The declared QEMU endpoint's availability (qemu-riscv64 with the CPU model declared in .env) is probed with the exact command and recorded as a Fact or Assumption.
The single source of truth for tool paths (the project .env) is identified in the recorded facts, and the environment summary is written to docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md.
No timing, speedup or performance measurement is recorded or required (correctness_only scope).

python3 -m compiler_agent --root . --json status lists recorded environment facts with confidence RUNTIME_PROBE or EMPIRICAL and no active UNKNOWN-confidence fact that blocks the build/run path
